claims.text: HandleAsync (or methods it calls) throws PoisonMessageException when the body is not valid JSON or not an order message, when the routing key has no email subject in SubjectFor, and when the message id is not a Guid.

OnReceivedAsync acknowledges after HandleAsync returns (74-75); on PoisonMessageException it logs a warning and calls BasicRejectAsync with requeue: false (77-81); on any other exception it logs an error and calls BasicNackAsync with requeue: true (82-86).
In C#, catch clauses are examined in order and the first one whose exception type matches handles the exception, so catch (PoisonMessageException) must precede catch (Exception).
claims.source_hint: C# language reference: Exception-handling statements > try-catch (order of catch clauses)

claims.text: RabbitMQ: a message rejected or nacked with requeue=false from a queue that has a dead-letter exchange is republished to that exchange (dead-lettered); without a dead-letter exchange it is discarded.
claims.source_hint: RabbitMQ docs: Dead Letter Exchanges > What is a Dead Letter Exchange / Configuration

claims.text: RabbitMQ: basic.nack or basic.reject with requeue=true returns the message to its queue, and it can be delivered again right away (no built-in wait). basic.nack with multiple=false does the same as basic.reject; nack only adds acting on several deliveries.
claims.source_hint: RabbitMQ docs: Consumer Acknowledgements and Publisher Confirms > Negative Acknowledgement and Requeuing of Deliveries

claims.text: RabbitMQ 4.1 quorum queues: x-delivery-limit caps how many times a message may be returned to the queue; a message returned more times than the limit is dead-lettered (or dropped when there is no dead-letter exchange). The delivery limit is a quorum queue feature.
claims.source_hint: RabbitMQ docs: Quorum Queues > Poison Message Handling; Queues > Optional Arguments

claims.text: A dead-lettered message keeps its original routing key when the queue sets no x-dead-letter-routing-key.
claims.source_hint: RabbitMQ docs: Dead Letter Exchanges > Routing Dead-Lettered Messages

claims.text: In a topic exchange binding, the pattern # matches every routing key.
claims.source_hint: RabbitMQ docs: Exchanges > Topic Exchange; prereq backend.l3.exchanges-and-bindings

claims.text: On dead-lettering, RabbitMQ adds headers to the message: x-death (an array of entries with queue, reason, count, exchange, among others), x-first-death-queue and x-first-death-reason; reason rejected means a consumer rejected it with requeue=false.
claims.source_hint: RabbitMQ docs: Dead Letter Exchanges > Dead-Lettered Messages (x-death header)

claims.text: RabbitMqTopology declares topic exchange notifications.dead-letter and queue notifications.order-events.dead (durable), bound with #; QueueArguments sets x-queue-type quorum, x-delivery-limit 5, x-dead-letter-exchange; line 26 passes it when declaring notifications.order-events.
At stage-3 no code consumes notifications.order-events.dead; it is read only by scripts/backend/dead-letter.sh and the test Running_PoisonMessage_EndsInTheDeadLetterQueue.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-3: git grep order-events.dead / DeadLetterQueue

claims.text: RabbitMQ does not move messages out of a queue by itself: a message in a queue with no consumer, no message TTL and no length limit stays until it is removed.
claims.source_hint: RabbitMQ docs: Queues; Time-To-Live and Expiration; Queue Length Limit (none set in RabbitMqTopology)

claims.text: The dead-letter exchange and queue live on the same RabbitMQ server as the main queue; docker-compose.yml at stage-3 has one rabbitmq service and none for the dead-letter queue.

dead-letter.sh empties notifications.order-events.dead, publishes order.placed with body 'this is not JSON' via the management API, waits for one message in the dead queue, then gets it with ackmode ack_requeue_false (removing it) and prints its headers.

Expected output of dead-letter.sh: routed: true (a queue received it, per the management API); 0 messages in notifications.order-events, 1 in .dead; routing_key order.placed, x-first-death-queue notifications.order-events, x-first-death-reason rejected, one x-death entry with count 1.

With x-delivery-limit 5 a requeued message's 6th failed delivery is its last, then it is dead-lettered (code comment; measured at /repo-stage 3); so the error log line repeats 6 times for one id, and requeue: true on a poison message costs 6 attempts.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-3: RabbitMqTopology.cs:39-44; DECISIONS.md 2026-10-06 /repo-stage 3 B1; RabbitMQ docs: Quorum Queues > Poison Message Handling

claims.text: The warning/error log lines are 'Rejecting message {MessageId}: {Reason}' and 'Handling message {MessageId} failed; returning it to the queue'.
Requeue a failed message only when the failure can pass (e.g. the database is down); reject a poison message without requeue, and cap requeues with a delivery limit so no message is retried forever.
claims.source_hint: outline items 1, 4; RabbitMQ docs: Quorum Queues > Poison Message Handling

claims.text: NotificationSender retries a failed email a fixed number of times, then sets the row to failed, which is never retried automatically.
